summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, chronic pancreatitis, atrial fibrillation, and type 2 diabetes was admitted for severe epigastric abdominal pain consistent with a flare of chronic pancreatitis. He presented with nausea, vomiting, and elevated lipase (226), but imaging showed no necrosis or complications. He was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and pain control, with gradual advancement to a regular diet. He developed transient delirium likely due to opioid and antihistamine use, which resolved with medication adjustment. His hemoglobin dropped from 8.8 to 7.5 g/dL but stabilized without active bleeding signs. Pulmonary edema and pleural effusions were noted on imaging, attributed to heart failure, and his oxygen needs improved. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to avoid combining hydroxyzine and diphenhydramine, monitor for GI bleeding, and follow up with his PCP for hemoglobin check at his next dialysis.
problems: Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled
